 USF Game Notes FIU Game Notes South Florida women's basketball forces 25 turnovers in 69-35 win over FIU
 November 15, 2026 | Women's Basketball
 Box Score Press Conference Photo Gallery Share: Amourie Porter scores 17 off the bench, and Kate Novik becomes a 1,000-point, 500-rebound player as South Florida improves to 4-1.
 TAMPA, Fla., November 15, 2026 – South Florida Women's Basketball forced a season-high 25 turnovers and held FIU to a season-low 35 points in a 69-35 win Sunday afternoon at the Yuengling Center, its 10th straight victory over the Panthers.
 Amourie Porter came off the bench to lead South Florida (4-1) with 17 points, her most as a Bull. She shot 5 for 8 from the field and made 7 of 8 free throws. Savannah Curry added 12 points in her first double-figure game as a Bull, and South Florida's reserves outscored FIU's 29-15. Hannah Kohn and Fatou Diakite scored 11 points apiece, and Stefanie Ingram had 10 points, seven rebounds and a game-high four assists to give South Florida five players in double figures.
 Kate Novik grabbed a game-high 11 rebounds, six on the offensive glass, to become a 1,000-point, 500-rebound player.
 How It Happened 
FIU scored six of the game's first eight points for a 6-2 lead, its largest of the day. Kohn's 3-pointer cut it to 6-5, and her layup with 1:35 left in the first quarter put South Florida ahead for good at 11-10. Ingram's jumper with two seconds left made it 13-10.
South Florida opened the second quarter on a 10-2 run, capped by Curry's 3-pointer for a 23-12 lead. FIU scored seven points in the quarter. Porter scored seven in its final 3:46 alone, and the Bulls closed the half on a 12-1 run to lead 35-17.
Diakite scored six of South Florida's first nine points of the third quarter, and Kohn's 3-pointer made it 44-19 with 5:18 left. Porter added six points in the period, and the Bulls took a 56-26 lead into the fourth.
Curry scored seven of her 12 points in the fourth quarter, and her 3-pointer with 1:37 left gave South Florida its largest lead of the season, 69-33.
South Florida shot 42.4% (25 of 59) and made 14 of 16 free throws. FIU shot 31.3% and made 2 of 17 from 3-point range. The Bulls outrebounded FIU 43-25, including 17-8 on the offensive glass, and outscored the Panthers 14-3 in fast-break points.
 Note-a-Bulls 
 South Florida has won 10 straight games against FIU and leads the series 15-8. FIU's last win came Dec. 18, 1996, in Tampa.
 FIU's 35 points were the fewest by a South Florida opponent this season; Furman's 54 in the opener had been the low. The Panthers' 17 first-half points, 18 second-half points, 31.3% shooting and 11.8% from 3-point range were also season lows for a Bulls opponent.
 South Florida's 25 forced turnovers were seven more than its previous high, at Belmont, and turned into 32 points. Its 13 steals matched the season high set against Furman. FIU entered with 27 steals in two games and finished with five.
 South Florida blocked five shots after blocking one in its first four games. Kendall Puryear had two blocks and three steals, tying her career highs in both.
 Kate Novik has 1,072 career points and 507 rebounds. Her 11 rebounds matched her high as a Bull, set at Belmont.
 Ingram's four assists gave her 204 at South Florida, passing Sydni Harvey (203) for No. 23 on the program's career list. She has 393 career assists, seven shy of 400, and her 181 last season rank fifth on the program's single-season list.
 Lisandra Vetesina grabbed her first career rebound.
 Up Next 
South Florida hosts Binghamton at 7 p.m. EST Wednesday at the Yuengling Center. The game will stream on ESPN+ and air on Bulls Unlimited. The Bearcats went 20-13 last season and reached the second round of the WNIT.

 About South Florida Women's Basketball 
 Kristy Curry  was named the seventh South Florida women's basketball head coach in program history. South Florida women's basketball has built a storied tradition over the past 25 seasons, highlighted by 19 postseason tournament appearances and 10 NCAA Tournament berths. The program has achieved 13 20-win seasons, two WNIT Final Four appearances, and captured the 2008-09 WNIT championship.
